_doc: THE ENSEMBLE — the Decibel piece's parts as notation data (container 6, 6.0, 2026-10-04 — RUNNING_LOG §45; the shape and every mechanism are piece #5's and #6's). Indexed by the composer score's LAYER, which is the IR's "part". Read by layout.js (clef, written pitch, staves), coords.js (the frame, the joined lane) and tools/notate_section.js.
_check: tools/notate_section.js refuses to extract when a part's `id` or `short` differs from the score's tracks[part] — the registry cannot drift from the composer score silently. The ids and shorts below are composer.html's TRACKS exactly; tools/palette_check.js guards the other direction.
_layersNote: composer.html: META_LAYER = 6 (= tracks.length), CURVE_LAYERS = [7, 8, 9] (the curve windows A / B / C, over the last three lanes — Mallets · Viola · Cello). Neither is a part; the extractor's default parts are 0 … 5. layoutVersion 8.
_transposeConvention: WRITTEN = SOUNDING + transpose semitones (layout.js line 75, and applied at line 965 — read in the code, not taken from a comment, during the port). The IR is always SOUNDING pitch (#5's D9); the shift happens at layout only, and the note is spelled from the written pitch. Piece #5's bass clarinet (+14, written a major ninth above sounding) is the precedent that fixes the sign.
_pitchForm: A TRANSPOSED score — the lineage's form, carried (piece #5: the bass clarinet in B♭, treble clef, his word 2026-09-11). Put to him 2026-10-04 as the one call of 6.0; his to reverse: "in C" is `transpose` removed from parts 0 and 1.

parts._transposeNote: The bass flute sounds an OCTAVE below written: written = sounding + 12, treble clef — the instrument's standard notation. Sounding range C3–D6 (MIDI 48–86, measured 2026-10-04) = written C4–D7.

B♭ bass clarinet in treble clef (the French notation — his word in piece #5, 2026-09-11, its RUNNING_LOG §382): written a major ninth (14 semitones) above sounding. The IR keeps SOUNDING pitch; the shift is applied at layout only.

lines.instrument: shime daiko (or a snare drum — PERFORMANCE_NOTES #5)

parts._staffNote: THE UNPITCHED STAFF, piece #6's type (after Ferneyhough's Bone Alphabet — one line per instrument, 2 ss apart, no clef, the short names in the gutter, a note ON the line of its instrument by its technique key's prefix): EIGHT lines here, for his TENTATIVE list of 2026-10-04 (COMPOSITION_NOTES DEC-6). THE ORDER IS PROVISIONAL AND THE AI'S — his rule of piece #6 applied as far as eight instruments allow ("high to low, no two neighbours of one material"): metal · skin · metal · skin · metal · skin · wood · skin. A staff type's design is HIS (the protocol's 6.2): put to him; reordering is this list.
parts._weightNote: The lane weight by piece #6's arithmetic: the brace [2, 3] is a JOINED group — one lane holding 14 ss (this staff) + 6 ss (the gap) + 4 ss (the mallets' staff) = 24 ss; extra = 20 ss over a unit lane; five lanes, A = (1080 − 16 − 4 × 4) / 7.9 = 132.66 ss, u = (A − 20) / 5 = 22.53, w = 1 + 20 / u = 1.888. Computed, not yet looked at on the page.

parts._clefNote: THE MALLETS — crotales · glockenspiel · xylophone · marimba, all four on this ONE five-line staff (his word, DEC-5). Treble clef, NO transposition in the registry: the Ricotti library maps every one of the four at its WRITTEN pitch (crotales C4–C6 · glockenspiel G3–C6 · xylophone F3–B6 · marimba C2–C7 as keyed), so the key the score sends IS the note to write — the crotales and the glockenspiel SOUND two octaves higher, the xylophone one, the marimba as written. Which instrument a note is for, and two at once ("opposite beaming or something like that"), is a DEVICE SHEET when the music reaches it (6.7). The marimba below middle C wants a bass clef; he is unlikely to use it. The part id is still "vibraphone" and the recipe key "bowed_vibraphone" — piece #6's, kept (docs/NAMING.md § 1).
Alto clef, as piece #5. A treble clef for a high stretch is the clefs-by-register item (the protocol's 6.10), not built.
Bass clef, as pieces #5 and #6. A tenor clef for a high stretch: 6.10, not built.

_groupsNote: Score order top to bottom: the two winds in a bracket · the ONE percussionist's two parts (Percussion, Mallets) in a BRACE, joined into one lane of the frame, 6 ss apart (piece #6's D12 and its 2a) · the two strings in a bracket. NO STAFF FOR THE ELECTRONICS (journal D8): every electronic sound is drawn on the staff of the player it comes from.
